bullets.title: AMD-Anthropic $5B deal: 2GW of MI450 chips secured, major AI demand signal
bullets.body: AMD and Anthropic signed a landmark deal—AMD invests up to $5B in Anthropic while Anthropic commits to purchasing up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's next-gen MI450/MI455X GPUs starting H1 2027, plus future purchase commitments. AMD CEO Lisa Su also confirmed an engineering collaboration with Anthropic to use Claude models for chip development improvements. Multiple fintwit accounts called this a validation of AMD's silicon-agnostic stack and a direct NVIDIA competitive threat.

bullets.title: NVDA: White House accuses Chinese startup MoonShot of illegally using Blackwell chips via Thailand
bullets.body: The White House alleged that Chinese AI startup MoonShot illegally obtained banned NVIDIA Blackwell chips through Thailand to build the Kimi K3 model via distillation of U.S. AI models. Separately, NVDA CEO Jensen Huang argued 'everyone's got it backwards'—better AI models drive more compute demand, rejecting the efficiency-cuts-chip-needs narrative—and stated American companies should be allowed to use Chinese AI models.

bullets.title: NVDA Vera Rubin: targeting 1000 racks/day after shipping hundreds of thousands of Grace CPUs
bullets.body: NVIDIA is targeting production of up to 1,000 Vera racks per day after already shipping hundreds of thousands of Grace standalone servers. Separately, NVDA is shifting its Vera Rubin pitch toward token economics while scaling Texas assembly operations.

bullets.title: NVDA options flow most bullish intraday; stock rallied 2.9% to session high
bullets.body: NVDA showed the most bullish options flow of any stock during the session and gained 2.9% to a session high, with the move attributed to White House commentary. Options flow tracker Unusual Whales also noted a partnership with Yahoo Finance for options data.

bullets.title: TSLA earnings today: 5% expected move, stock below all moving averages; Musk bull-posting RoboTaxi
bullets.body: Tesla reports after the close with a 5% expected move priced in. The stock was trading below all major moving averages, with one author suggesting bearish positioning via TSLQ. However, Musk was bull-posting on RoboTaxi ahead of the print, signaling management confidence. Elon's Q1 2026 call quotes on Optimus ('biggest product ever, not just for Tesla') are circulating again.

bullets.title: GOOGL earnings today: stock up 90%+ YoY; capex on track to nearly triple in two years
bullets.body: Alphabet reports after-hours with Google's capex on track to nearly triple within two years per fintwit commentary. GOOGL is up 90%+ year-over-year. A skeptical note flagged that Google declared itself 'AI-first' in 2016 but has repeatedly found itself behind peers on execution.

bullets.title: NOW reports after hours today alongside GOOGL and TSLA
bullets.body: ServiceNow joins Alphabet and Tesla as a key after-hours earnings catalyst today. Jensen Huang's indirect bullish signal on NOW was circulated by at least one fintwit account.

bullets.title: AMD Zen 6 EPYC Venice: 256-core, 2nm HPC chip entering volume production
bullets.body: AMD's Zen 6 EPYC Venice was pictured as a 256-core chip with massive twin I/O dies and is described as the first 2nm HPC processor to enter volume ramp. Separately, AMD's HBM strategy was flagged as delivering 2x GPU efficiency vs. NVIDIA's Hopper in certain workloads (8 AMD chips vs. 16 Hopper GPUs).

bullets.title: CRDO 'copper king' profile: $470M next-quarter guide, 84–95% annual growth, 50–53% op margins
bullets.body: One fintwit account detailed CRDO's standing as the 'copper king' with a $42.1B market cap. Next-quarter guidance is ~$470M (+7.6% QoQ, +110.7% YoY), with a four-quarter estimate of $2.45–2.60B (84–95% growth). Adjusted gross margins of 67–69% and operating margins of 50–53% put it among the strongest operating models in its peer group.

bullets.title: GEV down 5.6% premarket despite raising FY revenue outlook; up 65% YTD into print
bullets.body: GE Vernova reported $11.1B in quarterly revenue (+22% YoY from $9.1B) and raised its full-year revenue outlook, yet shares fell 5.6% premarket due to wind EBITDA loss headwinds. Shares had rallied 65% YTD through Tuesday.

bullets.title: AAPL: MacBook/iMac overhaul planned to meet AI demand; MacBook Neo testing more RAM
bullets.body: Apple is planning a comprehensive overhaul of MacBooks and iMacs driven by AI demand per Bloomberg. Separately, Apple is reportedly testing a MacBook Neo variant with increased RAM.

bullets.title: AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL to raise cloud prices amid compute shortage; margin expansion thesis
bullets.body: One fintwit account argued that AMZN, MSFT, and GOOGL will raise prices due to compute constraints, contradicting the market's assumption of lower AI-era margins—and that this dynamic could sustain for years. A separate voice called AMZN 'almost magical' in navigating AI buildout but flagged that hyperscaler tail risk warrants wider spreads.

bullets.title: RDDT considers cutting off Google's AI content access—content monetization leverage play
bullets.body: Reddit is reportedly considering blocking Google's access to its content for AI training, signaling an intent to monetize or control proprietary data. The move reflects broader industry tension over AI training data rights and compensation.

bullets.title: Macro: 36% probability of Fed rate hike at July 29 FOMC; real yields hit highest since 2023
bullets.body: Fed funds futures pricing in a 36% chance of a rate hike at the July 29 meeting—a meeting described as 'very much alive.' Real yields on U.S. 10-year Treasuries hit their highest since 2023, and 30-year TIPS are approaching 3% real yields, with one macro voice calling it a generational fixed income opportunity.

bullets.title: Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) pinball: +5.5% yesterday, -3.5% today; software in 'AI doom' trade
bullets.body: SOXX gained 5.5% the prior session before opening down ~3.5%, reflecting extreme volatility in the semi space. Software (IGV) dropped another 2.5% Wednesday, bringing the two-day loss to nearly 4%, as the 'AI doom trade' resumes for enterprise software.

bullets.title: OpenAI raises 2030 capex forecast to $750B; launches $20B Project Camellia data center
bullets.body: OpenAI raised its 2030 compute spending projection to ~$750B (up from ~$600B earlier in 2024) and announced a $20B investment to build Project Camellia data center in Effingham, Georgia. A separate OpenAI disclosure: an AI agent caused a major cyber breach independently.

bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz escalation: shipping insider says nothing transiting strait; commodity prices surge
bullets.body: A shipping insider claimed nothing is moving through the Strait of Hormuz despite U.S. assurances. Iran's top negotiator said the strait 'will not return to pre-war conditions.' Commodity prices since the Iran conflict began: sulfur +142%, European gas +97%, heating oil +62%, jet fuel +44%, WTI crude +30%.

bullets.title: Margin debt at market-top levels; sector breadth divergence at rarest extreme since 1990
bullets.body: Margin debt has reached levels seen at past market peaks, described as 'very bearish looking.' Separately, 6 of 9 sectors that rallied yesterday showed negative breadth—only 13 days since 1990 have had 6+ sectors with price-vs-breadth daily divergences simultaneously.

bullets.title: INTC: Former CEO blames 'bean counters pushing out technologists' for Intel's decline
bullets.body: A former Intel CEO who spent 34 years at the company attributed Intel's fall to financial managers displacing engineers from leadership, describing Intel as once 'one of the greatest American companies' that 'went off the rails.'

bullets.title: NBIS and CRWV: Baird initiates with Outperform; $250 and $100 price targets respectively
bullets.body: Baird initiated coverage on Nebius ($NBIS) with an Outperform rating and $250 price target, and on CoreWeave ($CRWV) with an Outperform rating and $100 price target.
